subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'Exact piece of land that a settlement is built on.' (Y: situation / Z: site)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (site) (1 mark)
Site refers to the exact/actual piece of land on which a settlement is built, whereas situation refers to the location of a settlement in relation to its surroundings.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'The situation of a commercial livestock farm is influenced by …' (Y: topography / Z: markets)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (markets) (1 mark)
The situation of a commercial livestock farm is influenced by its access to markets, since commercial farming is profit-driven and needs to sell produce.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'Settlements located close to a water source in arid areas.' (Y: wet-point / Z: dry-point)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (wet-point) (1 mark)
Wet-point settlements locate close to a water source, which is especially important in arid areas where water is scarce.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'The shape of this settlement is influenced by a river.' (Y: circular / Z: linear)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (linear) (1 mark)
A settlement whose shape is influenced by a river is arranged in a line along the river, giving it a linear shape.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'The largest rural settlement type.' (Y: village / Z: hamlet)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (village) (1 mark)
A village is a larger rural settlement type than a hamlet, which is one of the smallest.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'Greater profits are associated with this settlement pattern.' (Y: dispersed / Z: nucleated)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (dispersed) (1 mark)
A dispersed settlement pattern (farmsteads spread far apart on large landholdings) is associated with extensive commercial farming and greater profits.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'Land returned to the original owners.' (Y: land restitution / Z: land tenure)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (land restitution) (1 mark)
Land restitution is the programme that returns land to the original/rightful owners who were dispossessed, while land tenure refers to how land is held or owned.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'An economic challenge of land reform.' (Y: poverty / Z: legal disputes)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y/Z (1 mark)
The official marking guideline accepts EITHER Y (poverty) OR Z (legal disputes) as a valid economic challenge of land reform.

subQuestions.questionText: The smallest urban settlement in an urban hierarchy is a …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (town) (1 mark)
Of the options given, a town is the smallest urban settlement type in the urban hierarchy (below a city, metropolis and megalopolis).

subQuestions.questionText: A … has the smallest number of settlements.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (megalopolis) (1 mark)
A megalopolis is the highest order in the urban hierarchy and there are very few of them, so it has the smallest number of settlements.

subQuestions.questionText: A … is the largest settlement type found in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (conurbation) (1 mark)
A conurbation is the largest settlement type found in South Africa (a megalopolis does not occur in South Africa).

subQuestions.questionText: A … is an urban settlement type made up of a major city and towns.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (metropolis) (1 mark)
A metropolis is an urban settlement type made up of a major city together with the surrounding towns that have grown together.

subQuestions.questionText: The … of a city covers a larger area than a town.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (sphere of influence) (1 mark)
The sphere of influence (the area served by a settlement) of a city is larger than that of a town because a city offers more, higher-order goods and services.

subQuestions.questionText: A university has a … range and a … sphere of influence than a school.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (larger; larger) (1 mark)
A university offers a high-order service, so people travel further to reach it (larger range) and it serves a larger area (larger sphere of influence) than a school.

subQuestions.questionText: The range associated with the purchase of a motor vehicle is greater than the purchase of bread because it is: (i) More expensive (ii) Purchased on a daily basis (iii) Not purchased frequently (iv) Less expensive
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A ((i) and (iii)) (1 mark)
A motor vehicle is a high-order good with a large range because it is more expensive (i) and it is not purchased frequently (iii), so people are willing to travel further to buy it.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketch and graph showing the levels of poverty caused by rural-urban migration. Define the term rural-urban migration.
subQuestions.memoText:
Concept (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Movement of people from rural areas to urban areas (2)
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PART MARKING: Movement of people from rural areas (1).

subQuestions.questionText: According to the graph, the percentage level of poverty decreased by a smaller amount in (rural/urban) areas.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: rural (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
The graph shows that the percentage level of poverty decreased by a smaller amount in rural areas.

subQuestions.questionText: How has unemployment contributed to this trend in poverty levels (answer to QUESTION 1.3.2)?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- People earn no/low salaries (2)
- They are not able to afford basic services (accept examples) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: How does the movement of young adults to urban areas have a negative social impact on the rural community?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Birth rate declines (2)
- Ageing population (2)
- Disruption to family units (accept examples) (2)
- Increase in poverty (2)
- Increase in unemployment (2)
- Decrease in (access to) services (accept examples) (2)
- Standard of living decreases (accept examples) (2)
- Older/younger community members vulnerable to social ills (accept examples) (2)
- Gender structure changes (2)
- Quality of life decreases (accept examples) (2)
- Brain drain as skilled people leave rural area (2)
- Loss of community identity (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest strategies that can be introduced in rural areas to reduce the movement of young adults to urban areas.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY THREE of the following (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
- Create opportunities for investments (accept examples) (2)
- Increase employment opportunities (accept examples) (2)
- Skills development programmes (accept examples) (2)
- Promote entrepreneurship (2)
- Develop community projects (2)
- Make services more accessible (accept examples) (2)
- Improve the quality of services (accept examples) (2)
- Improve infrastructure (accept examples) (2)
- Increase recreational/cultural activities (accept examples) (2)
- Promote tourism (accept examples) (2)
- Subsidising education (2)
- Land reform programmes (accept examples) (2)
- Young farmers receive financial assistance (accept examples) (2)
- Provide market-related salaries/bonuses (accept examples) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketch showing an urban profile. Define the concept urban profile.
subQuestions.memoText:
Concept (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Side view of an urban area (2)
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PART MARKING: Side view (1).

subQuestions.questionText: Comment on the height of buildings in the CBD in comparison to those in the rural-urban fringe.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- Height of buildings decreases (1)
- Height of buildings increases towards the CBD (1)
- Buildings are taller in the CBD/lower in the rural-urban fringe (1)

subQuestions.questionText: How has the demand for land influenced the density of buildings in the CBD?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Resulted in a high building density (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why are both the transition zone and rural-urban fringe referred to as zones of change?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Characterised by mixed land use (2)
- Invasion and succession (accept examples) (2)
- Urban renewal occurs (2)
- Urban expansion/urban sprawl occurs (accept examples) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest economic reasons why the rural-urban fringe would be an attractive location for commercial activities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY THREE of the following (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
- Land is cheaper (2)
- Available land (2)
- Accessible market (2)
- Reduced transport costs (accept examples) (2)
- Accessible transport infrastructure (accept examples) (2)
- Less costs incurred due to less crime (accept examples) (2)
- Access to raw materials (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the photographs and extract on informal settlements. Define the term informal settlement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Concept (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Building of structures on land that people occupy with no legal claim (2)
(Accept shacks that are erected from different building materials on vacant land / temporary / unplanned settlements / no basic services) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE factor in the extract that has a negative impact on the health of residents in informal settlements.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- Lack of basic services (1)
- Pollution (1)
- Overcrowding (1)
- Poor waste management (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO economic reasons for the increase in informal settlements.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Municipal budgets cannot keep up with the increasing demand (2)
- High levels of unemployment/lower wages (2)
- High levels of poverty (2)
- Unaffordable formal housing/rent (2)
- Difficulty in obtaining financial assistance (accept examples) (2)
- High interest rates (2)
- Cheaper to rent/build (accept examples) (2)
- Closer proximity to work (2)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain how the upgrading (improvement) of informal settlements would have a positive social impact for people living in these settlements.
subQuestions.memoText:
PARAGRAPH question. Award 2 marks each for ANY FOUR of the following (4 x 2 = 8 marks):
- Improved services (accept examples) improve quality of life (2)
- More facilities (accept examples) built for greater convenience (2)
- Improved transport infrastructure will link surrounding areas to allow for accessibility (accept examples) (2)
- Upgraded infrastructure (accept examples) improves quality of life (2)
- Better access to recreational facilities (accept examples) to improve quality of life (2)
- Community networks (accept examples) are preserved lowering levels of crime (2)
- Aesthetics/healthier environment (accept examples) improves life expectancy (2)
- Building social capital will create a sense of community belonging (2)
- Teach locals new skills (accept examples) that could ensure employment (2)
- Appointment of local people creates job opportunities (2)
[MAXIMUM OF FOUR MARKS]

subQuestions.questionText: The main difference between small-scale and large-scale farming is the …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (size of farm holdings) (1 mark)
The main difference between small-scale and large-scale farming is the size of the farm holdings.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the photographs on small- and large-scale farming. Photograph … illustrates small-scale farming.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (photograph S) (1 mark)
Photograph S illustrates small-scale farming.

subQuestions.questionText: A characteristic of small-scale farming evident in the photograph is …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (the use of manual labour) (1 mark)
Small-scale farming, as shown in the photograph, is characterised by the use of manual labour rather than heavy machinery.

subQuestions.questionText: … is an economic advantage for a farmer practising large-scale farming.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (Larger profits) (1 mark)
Larger profits are an economic advantage of large-scale (commercial) farming. The use of machinery, a large labour force and monoculture are methods/features rather than economic advantages.

subQuestions.questionText: Cattle farming is an activity in the … economic sector.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (primary) (1 mark)
Cattle farming involves the extraction/production of raw materials from nature, which is a primary sector activity.

subQuestions.questionText: Distribution of dairy products is an activity in the … economic sector.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (tertiary) (1 mark)
Distribution (a service that moves goods to the consumer) is a tertiary sector activity.

subQuestions.questionText: A factor favouring cattle farming in South Africa is …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (available grazing land) (1 mark)
The availability of grazing land favours cattle farming in South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Challenges faced by small-scale cattle farmers in South Africa are: (i) High rate of unemployment (ii) Animal diseases (iii) Semi-arid land (iv) Export market
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B ((ii) and (iii)) (1 mark)
Animal diseases (ii) and semi-arid land (iii) are the challenges faced by small-scale cattle farmers in South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'The main purpose of an industrial development zone (IDZ) is to promote …' (Y: exports / Z: imports)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (exports) (1 mark)
The main purpose of an industrial development zone (IDZ) is to promote exports.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'SDIs are generally located in … areas.' (Y: underdeveloped / Z: developed)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (underdeveloped) (1 mark)
Spatial development initiatives (SDIs) are generally located in underdeveloped areas in order to stimulate development there.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'A positive economic impact of spatial development initiatives (SDIs) is …' (Y: improved quality of life / Z: upgraded infrastructure)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (upgraded infrastructure) (1 mark)
Upgraded infrastructure is a positive economic impact of SDIs, while improved quality of life is a social impact.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'A social challenge experienced in the Saldanha Bay IDZ is …' (Y: unskilled workforce / Z: poor harbour facilities)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (unskilled workforce) (1 mark)
An unskilled workforce is a social challenge in the Saldanha Bay IDZ, whereas poor harbour facilities would be a physical/economic challenge.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'The main industry associated with the West Coast SDI is a/an …' (Y: automotive plant / Z: steel plant)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (steel plant) (1 mark)
The main industry associated with the West Coast SDI is a steel plant (Saldanha Steel).

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'The South-western Cape core industrial region is restricted by …' (Y: few mineral resources / Z: small local markets)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (few mineral resources) (1 mark)
The South-western Cape core industrial region is restricted by its few mineral resources.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option in COLUMN B (write only Y or Z): 'A physical factor that promotes industries in the South-western Cape core industrial region is …' (Y: overseas markets / Z: coastal location)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (coastal location) (1 mark)
A coastal location is a physical factor that promotes industries in the South-western Cape core industrial region (overseas markets is an economic, not physical, factor).

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the graph and extract on coal mining in South Africa. According to the graph, what amount of coal, in billions, was exported in 2023?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: (R)250 (billion) (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
According to the graph, R250 billion worth of coal was exported in 2023.

subQuestions.questionText: What has been the general trend in profits from the export of coal in recent years?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- There is an upward/increasing/positive trend (1)
(Accept figures that indicate an increase in exports) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the graph, between which years was the smallest number of employees recorded in the coal mining industry?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Between 2021 and 2022 (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
The graph shows the smallest number of employees was recorded between 2021 and 2022.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE possible reason for the small number of employees (answer to QUESTION 2.3.3).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Depletion of coal (2)
- Economic recession (accept examples) (2)
- Impact of illness/pandemics (accept examples) (2)
- Possible strikes/uprisings (accept examples) (2)
- Increase in mechanisation (2)
- Threats of nationalisation (accept examples) (2)

- Load-shedding (2)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the extract, the high-quality coal reserves in South Africa have been decreasing over the years. Explain the negative impact of decreasing high-quality coal reserves for the future supply of power in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):

- There would be a greater demand than supply (2)
- The cost of electricity would increase (accept examples) (2)

- Expensive to invest in alternative energy sources (accept examples) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the coal mining industry is important to the economy of South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY THREE of the following (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
- It creates employment opportunities thus reducing dependency on government/increasing the buying power of people (2)
- Multiplier effect stimulates other industries growing the economy (2)
- Coal mining contributes to the GDP that stimulates the economy (2)

- The use of coal as a raw material to manufacture other products (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the infographic on the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region. Refer to the statistics and state the percentage that the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region contributes to the GDP of South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the topographical map. Calculate the average gradient from spot height 1358 at G in block A3 to trigonometrical station 96 at H in block C4. Use the following information: The distance between spot height 1358 and trigonometrical station 96 is 7,8 cm. Formula: Gradient = Vertical Interval (VI) / Horizontal Equivalent (HE).
subQuestions.memoText:
Average gradient (4 x 1 = 4 marks):
VI = 1455,6 m − 1358 m = 97,6 m (1)
HE = 7,8 cm x 500 = 3 900 m (1)
Gradient = VI / HE = 97,6 / 3 900 (1 mark for substitution)
= 1 : 39,96 (1) (accept 1 : 40)

subQuestions.questionText: Is the gradient (answer to QUESTION 3.1.5) steep or gentle?
